leaseNotes.label: Co-tenancy
leaseNotes.value: During the Term, if Home Depot (HD) ceases to operate and does not recommence — or is not replaced by a comparable user — within 90 days, Tenant may pay 2% of Gross Sales in lieu of Base Rent, OR terminate on 90 days' notice. (Lease §14.20, 4/21/2003)

leaseNotes.label: Exclusive Use
leaseNotes.value: No part of the Center may be used for the sale/leasing of business or office equipment (incl. computers & telecom), furniture or supplies, or business/office services (copying, printing, telecom, packing, shipping, equipment repair) — the "Exclusive Goods and Services." No Landlord-owned property within one mile may be used as an "office supply superstore." Exceptions: existing tenants in permitted uses as of the Lease date; future tenants selling Exclusive Goods/Services incidental to their primary business (≤10% of sales-floor area); Radio Shack, Hallmark, Chuck E Cheese, Best Buy; Wal-Mart and Home Depot. (Lease §5.2.1 & §5.3, 4/21/2003)

leaseNotes.label: LL Restrictions
leaseNotes.value: Prohibited Uses [A]. Prohibited tire-store use partially WAIVED for the NTB Parcel (Outparcel 1) only, for NTB or affiliates only, max 8,000 SF (1st Amendment §6, 12/15/2016). Restricted Use: no part of the Center within 120 ft of the Premises may be a restaurant (except one restaurant ≤3,500 SF permitted within 200 ft but not within 60 ft of the Premises).

leaseNotes.label: Go Dark Option
leaseNotes.value: Tenant may go dark (no continuous-operation covenant). Landlord RECAPTURE: if Tenant ceases to operate for more than 12 consecutive months (excluding casualty/alterations/renovation/repairs), Landlord may terminate on 90 days' notice given within 60 days after the 12-month period; if not exercised, Landlord gets additional 60-day windows after each subsequent 6-month period of non-operation. On termination Landlord pays Tenant the unamortized cost of leasehold improvements less the unamortized Improvement Contribution. (Lease §5.4 & §5.4.1, 4/21/2003)

leaseNotes.label: Assignment & Sublet
leaseNotes.value: Tenant may assign or sublet all or any portion of the Premises and grant licenses/concessions WITHOUT Landlord consent, provided Tenant remains primarily liable. After any assignment by the original Tenant, Landlord must notify the original Tenant of any claimed default. (Lease §9.1, 4/21/2003)

flags.issue: Co-tenancy tied to Home Depot — single-anchor dependency
flags.detail: If Home Depot goes dark and isn't recommenced/replaced by a comparable user within 90 days, Staples can drop to 2% of Gross Sales in lieu of Base Rent OR terminate on 90 days' notice. Losing Home Depot alone trips this — monitor HD's status and confirm whether HD is an owned anchor or a separate-parcel (shadow) box. (Lease §14.20)

No continuous-operation covenant, so Staples can go dark; but if it ceases operating >12 consecutive months, Landlord may recapture on 90 days' notice — and must then pay unamortized TI less the unamortized Improvement Contribution. Models a re-tenanting cost on recapture. (Lease §5.4)

Constrains future leasing/merchandising. Carve-outs include Wal-Mart and Home Depot. (Lease §5.2.1, §5.3)

abstracts.narrative: Staples is a junior-anchor box at Main Street Station. Its rent is exposed to Home Depot via an operating co-tenancy: if HD goes dark and isn't replaced by a comparable user within 90 days, Staples can pay just 2% of gross sales in lieu of base rent or walk on 90 days' notice — a meaningful single-anchor dependency. The lease carries a very broad office/business-supply exclusive (Center-wide plus a 1-mile superstore radius) that constrains future leasing, an uncommonly tenant-favorable no-consent assignment right, and a landlord go-dark recapture (>12 months, with a TI true-up). Sales reporting is required only while co-tenancy relief is in effect. ROFR/ROFO and radius are silent. All terms are summary-sourced and unverified — confirm the 2003 lease + amendment chain (a 2016 1st Amendment is referenced).

leaseNotes.label: Co-tenancy
leaseNotes.value: Ongoing co-tenancy with Wal-Mart. On a Co-Tenancy Failure, Base Rent is reduced 50% for as long as the failure continues. If the failure continues 365 consecutive days, Tenant may terminate on 90 days' notice. If it continues 540 consecutive days, then within 30 days of Landlord notice Tenant must either terminate (lease ends 60 days after notice) or resume full Base Rent; failing to elect within the 30-day period waives termination and Tenant resumes Base Rent the next day. "Comparable replacement" = a national/regional chain then operating ≥50 US stores in a use not prohibited by the lease; up to 3 replacements may occupy ≥75% of the co-tenant's gross floor area and use ≥90% of its frontage. (Lease, Exhibit E, p.67, §1-5)

leaseNotes.label: Exclusive Use
leaseNotes.value: Tenant's primary business of selling (on an incidental basis) pet food, pet accessories and pet products. Does not apply to Wal-Mart, Staples and Home Depot. On a violation uncured 30 days after notice, Tenant may abate rent until the violation ceases, or terminate at any time before cessation. (Lease, Exhibit G, p.73, §2)

leaseNotes.label: Go Dark Option

Affiliate transfers permitted without consent so long as Tenant remains PetSmart Inc. For a third-party (non-affiliate) assignment/sublease, Landlord may terminate and recapture on 30 days' notice (lease ends 90 days after the 30-day period). (Lease p.31, §16.2)

abstracts.narrative: PetSmart is a junior anchor whose economics hinge on Wal-Mart. Its operating co-tenancy cuts base rent 50% the moment Wal-Mart goes dark, ripens into a termination right at 365 days, and forces a terminate-or-pay election at 540 days — a real, single-anchor exposure. It also holds a pet-goods exclusive with an abatement/termination remedy and a credit-based assignment right (no consent to investment-grade assignees), against which Landlord retains a recapture on third-party transfers and a 180-day go-dark recapture. Because Wal-Mart simultaneously anchors the PetSmart, GameStop and Rent-A-Center co-tenancies, confirming Wal-Mart's ownership/lease status and term is the single most important diligence item for this center. Radius is silent. Summary-sourced — verify the executed lease, Exhibit E and Exhibit G.
